    AI Overview
    +5
    The Ambassador Bridge is a 7,500-foot (1.4-mile) international suspension bridge connecting Detroit, Michigan, and Windsor, Ontario. Opened in 1929, it is a critical trade link but, as of 2025–2026, it is no longer the busiest commercial crossing, having been surpassed by the Blue Water Bridge in Sarnia. It remains a top passenger vehicle route, operating 24/7. 
    Key Details About the Ambassador Bridge 
    • Location: Connects Detroit, Michigan (USA) and Windsor, Ontario (Canada).
    • Traffic Trends (2026): In 2025 and early 2026, the Blue Water Bridge in Sarnia overtook the Ambassador Bridge for commercial truck traffic.
    • Tolls & Costs: Commercial truck tolls are approximately
      per axle, while passenger tolls are lower, contributing to the shift in truck traffic to other crossings.
    • Significance: It serves as a major trade artery for the U.S. and Canada, with its construction completed in 1929.
    • Length: The total structure spans 7,500 feet (2,286 m).
    • Ownership: The bridge is privately owned by the Detroit International Bridge Company. 
    History and Design 
    • Opening Date: The bridge officially opened on November 11, 1929.
    • Record: At its construction, it was the world's largest suspension bridge.
    • Design: It was designed by Jonathan Jones and features a 1,850-foot suspended central span. 
    Traffic & Commercial Information 
    • Commercial Traffic (2025/2026): While previously the busiest, 2025 saw about 1.9 million truck crossings compared to over 2.1 million at the Blue Water Bridge.
    • Passenger Traffic: The bridge remains popular for passenger vehicles, handling 3.5 million such vehicles in 2025.
    • Hours: Open 24/7.

    Opening Date. When was the Ambassador Bridge built?
    Feedback
    1929
    Construction began in 1927 and was completed in 1929. The general contractor and steel erector was the McClintic-Marshall Company of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The bridge is made up of 21,000 short tons (19,000 tonnes) of steel, and the roadway rises as high as 152 feet (46 m) above the Detroit River.

    What was the Ambassador Bridge originally called?
    The total cost of the project was $23.5 million. During its construction, the bridge was called the Detroit River Bridge. Bower felt that the name was too impersonal but did not want the bridge named after him, so he named it the Ambassador Bridge.

    Is the Ambassador Bridge the longest bridge?
    Design. The bridge over the Detroit River had the longest suspended central span in the world when it was completed in 1929—1,850 feet (560 m). This record held until the George Washington Bridge between New York and New Jersey opened in 1931. The bridge's total length is 7,500 feet (2,286 m).
